title: IT stocks lift Sensex by 390 points; Nifty ends above 25,880
summary: Thursday's early weakness gave way to a technology-led recovery. The benchmarks closed higher for a second session, even as banks and consumer shares slipped.

sections.heading: IT takes the reins
sections.body: The Sensex added 390.31 points to finish at 84,328.59 on Thursday, while the Nifty 50 gained 65.25 points to close at 25,884.50. After Wednesday’s consumer-led rebound, the leadership shifted to technology companies. HCL Technologies rose roughly 6%, while TCS and Infosys both gained more than 4%, Reuters reported.

sections.heading: A mixed day beneath the headlines
sections.body: The Nifty IT index climbed 3.66% and realty shares advanced 3.27%, according to Liquide's closing report. Metals also gained ground. Banks moved the other way: Bank Nifty closed at 63,535.30, down 0.26%. Consumer durables and FMCG recorded losses of 1.33% and 0.94%, respectively. Upstox reported that only 22 Nifty 50 constituents finished higher, with 28 declining.

sections.heading: Oil and foreign buying remain in focus
sections.body: The recovery came as crude prices eased from their intraday highs. Reuters reported that foreign portfolio purchases had helped drive the broader November rally. Investors continued to track US trade policy and developments overseas. Thursday's closing levels tell only part of the story; the narrower participation is worth keeping in mind.

sections.heading: Welspun Corp reports fresh orders
sections.body: The pipe manufacturer disclosed about ₹2,264 crore in additional orders secured since its October 29 announcement, taking its global order book to around ₹50,000 crore, according to Financial Express. The update included an export order for longitudinal submerged arc welded pipes.

sections.heading: Foodlink opens its public issue
sections.body: Foodlink F&B Holdings opened its initial public offering on Thursday. Kotak Neo reported an issue size of ₹360.76 crore and a price band of ₹181–₹191 a share. The subscription window is scheduled to close on November 30.
